So I was over on reddit when voat was down and I mentioned this subverse. I got a few PMs from people who wanted to check it out! Some of them seasoned writers, some of them just learning. So I figured...

"Huh, well, we need an introduction thread so people aren't so scared of the maybe 5 active users. A place where people can go to voice out who they are, how they started wanting to write, and their apprehensions. Also a place where people can state what they're wanting to work on!"

Don't worry guys. We're actually pretty friendly! We focus on positive, constructive criticism. From my experience, we also try not to downvoat. That's discouraging to a lot of new writers, who are already apprehensive about posting in the first place!

So let me introduce myself: I'm gr33narrow. I'm no one important, just a person who likes to write and read other people's submissions. I started writing ever since I learned the alphabet, and I hadn't stopped untiiilllll..... one day, I got hit pretty damn hard with depression and anxiety. Like, we're talking Sometimes calling into work, laying around, not doing anything. And I lost my creative spark. Welp, that lasted four years and I got sick of it, so A few months ago, I decided to ease myself back into it - yayyy!!!! Now I'm a posting fiend!

PromptoftheDay really has helped me focus. The mods, @raisin and @SurvivorType are super cool peeps. They offer me the feedback I need to either keep going, or rethink. The things I'm most self conscious about are my writer's voice (it's pretty blatantly me) and my character dialogue. I have to constantly remind myself that not everyone speaks with proper grammar, a sort of folksy accent, and how I need to describe certain things about voices (Are they gruff? Soft? raspy?). This is great practice, and a wonderful way to work out some kinks in my writing.

So, tell me a little bit about yourself. What's your story (pun intended)? What do you feel like you need help with? Don't be shy. You don't have to start working right away. Just give a brief (or not brief) intro and it'll all be groovy! Go start reading, check out the prompts, read the comments. Get ideas. Oh --- and I learned that the max character limit for a post is 10,000 characters (text characters,not story characters. But if you do have 10,000 characters in your story you might have a hard time keeping up....).

Rock on! I'll be here. Not a mod, but your friendly subverse fellow citizen! No longer applicable

As for the rules of why on magic, I have a suggestion. Well, more of a personal observation. I forget what the actual name is called, but there is a thing about when a book (Movie, story, whatever) fails to follow the rules it has established. Things like plot armor, 'because science/magic!', and other bad writing tropes are related to this. What makes things easier for me, is to clearly establish these universe rules for yourself, say on a piece of paper. Edit these as needed, but make sure your content holds true to these tenants. As you write more and refine this list of rules, you will (hopefully) start making connections between your story and these rules. "Why does this magic do X?" > "Because it follows X rule" > "What does that mean in the terms of the story?" sort of thing.
